items.title: Carrier-Aware Sound Zone Control for Parametric Array Loudspeakers
items.authors: Mengtong Li(Nanjing University); Tao Zhuang(Nanjing University); Yu Sun(Samsung Electronics (China)); Shaozhe Li(Nanjing University); Xuxiang Wu(Nanjing University); Jia-Xin Zhong(Nanjing University); Jing Lu(Nanjing University; Horizon Robotics)
items.abstract: Parametric array loudspeakers (PALs) exploit ultrasonic carrier and nonlinear self-demodulation to generate directional speech and audio sound, offering advantages for spatial audio reproduction. While recent work extends linear-acoustic sound zone control (SZC) to PAL arrays by optimizing sideband excitations and achieves high acoustic contrast (AC), the carrier--essential for demodulation--remains unexplored as a control variable. We propose a carrier-aware SZC framework for PALs, treating the carrier as a new control dimension, with an alternating optimization for sideband and carrier weights. Simulations and experiments show that our method outperforms sideband-only control, yielding higher AC and demodulation efficiency. In experiments, broadband gains of 11.2 dB in AC and 7.0 dB in target-zone SPL are achieved under identical power constraints. The results establish the carrier as a key control variable for more efficient, high-performance spatial audio and speech rendering with PALs.

items.title: A Sparsity-Aware Robust Nonlinear Active Noise Control for Impulsive Noise Environments
items.authors: Hengwei Xu(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Hongqing Liu(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Liming Shi(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Lu Gan(Brunel University)
items.abstract: Functional link network (FLN) based active noise control (ANC) alogorithms offer strong nonlinear modeling capabilities but inevitably introduce redundant basis functions during expansion, leading to inefficient adaptation and degraded steady-state performance. To improve the performance, we propose a sparsity-aware robust nonlinear ANC algorithm that incorporates a reweighted zero-attracting (RZA) regularization term into the minimum-output-variance constrained filtered-s least mean p-power (MOV-FsLMP) framework. This mechanism acts as an online feature selector, effectively suppressing redundant coefficients induced by FLN expansion while preserving the inherent robustness against impulsive disturbances. Extensive simulations under α-state impulsive noise conditions demonstrate that the proposed algorithm consistently outperforms the conventional MOV-FsLMP, achieving a 1-2 dB improvement in steady-state mean square error (MSE) and a higher active noise reduction (ANR) under identical configurations, validating its practical effectiveness for nonlinear ANC applications.

items.title: NCPSZ: A Nonlinear Control Network for Miniature Loudspeakers in Personal Sound Zone Applications
items.authors: Chen Gong(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Lei Zhou(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Chen Huang(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Hongqing Liu(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Liming Shi(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Lu Gan(Brunel University)
items.abstract: In personal sound zone (PSZ) systems, linear control methods suffer from significant performance degradation on devices with miniature loudspeakers due to severe nonlinear distortion (NLD). To overcome this limitation, we propose a nonlinear control network for PSZ (NCPSZ), a data-driven framework tailored for sound leakage prevention. We introduce an asymmetric dual-network architecture: a high-fidelity modeling network (ModelNet) characterizes the loudspeaker's nonlinear behavior offline, which supervises a lightweight, causal control network (CtrlNet) for real-time operation. Crucially, we employ an "anchor speaker" strategy, where the primary earpiece speaker maintains the target sound pressure in the bright zone (BZ), while the CtrlNet optimizes assisting speakers to actively cancel nonlinear leakage in the dark zone (DZ). Validated in a realistic smartphone leakage-prevention task, NCPSZ achieves a consistent acoustic contrast (AC) improvement of 3.78 dB over the linear VAST baseline and 1.80 dB over a parameter-matched causal CNN, demonstrating effective privacy protection under nonlinear regimes.

items.title: LMPAN: A Lightweight Multi-Path Alignment Network for Joint Full-Duplex Acoustic Echo Cancellation and Noise Suppression
items.authors: Chengwei Liu(Alibaba); Shaofei Xue(Alibaba); Haoyin Yan(Alibaba); Xiaotao Liang(Alibaba); Zheng Xue(Qwen Business Unit of Alibaba)
items.abstract: We propose a lightweight multi-path alignment network (LMPAN) for on-device joint acoustic echo cancellation (AEC) and noise suppression (NS) in full-duplex spoken dialogue systems. To address hardware-induced distortions and dynamic acoustic conditions, we introduce three core innovations: (1) a multi-path alignment stage correcting temporal and energy mismatches across reference, linear AEC (LAEC) output, and microphone signals; (2) an attention-based mechanism that dynamically integrates enhanced LAEC and microphone features under varying acoustic scenarios; (3) a post-filtering module with a dynamic target generation strategy for downstream tasks (ASR, VAD). Furthermore, we adopt a two-stage training framework leveraging self-supervised learning representations to enhance perceptual quality. Experiments show that LMPAN, with only 480K parameters and 126 MACs, achieves performance comparable to the state-of-the-art lightweight model DeepVQE-S, while ensuring real-time inference capability.

items.title: Active Constructive Interference for Speech
items.authors: Ofir Yaish(Ben-Gurion University of the Negev); Yehuda Mishaly(Tel Aviv University); Eliya Nachmani(Ben-Gurion University of the Negev)
items.abstract: We introduce a new paradigm for active sound modification: Active Speech Enhancement (ASE). While Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) algorithms focus on suppressing external interference and traditional speech enhancement passively reconstructs degraded speech signals, ASE goes further by actively shaping the speech signal, both attenuating distortions and amplifying speech-relevant frequencies to improve intelligibility and perceptual quality. To enable this, we propose a novel Transformer-Mamba-based architecture, along with a task-specific loss function that jointly optimizes interference suppression and signal enrichment in an acoustic environment. Our method outperforms existing baselines across multiple speech processing tasks, including denoising, dereverberation, and declipping, demonstrating the effectiveness of active, targeted modulation in challenging acoustic environments. A demo and code are publicly available at github.com/ofiryaish/ASE-TM.

items.title: Predictive Directional Selective Fixed-Filter Active Noise Control for Moving Sources via a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network
items.authors: Boxiang Wang(Nanyang Technological University); Zhengding Luo(Nanyang Technological University); Dongyuan Shi(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Junwei Ji(Nanyang Technological University); Xiruo Su(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Woon-Seng Gan(Nanyang Technological University)
items.abstract: Directional Selective Fixed-Filter Active Noise Control (D-SFANC) can effectively attenuate noise from different directions by selecting the suitable pre-trained control filter based on the Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) of the current noise. However, this method is weak at tracking the direction variations of non-stationary noise, such as that from a moving source. Therefore, this work proposes a Predictive Directional SFANC (PD-SFANC) method that uses a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) to capture the hidden temporal dynamics of the moving noise and predict the control filter to cancel future noise. Accordingly, the proposed method can significantly improve its noise-tracking ability and dynamic noise-reduction performance. Furthermore, numerical simulations confirm the superiority of the proposed method for handling moving sources across various movement scenarios, compared to several representative ANC baselines.

items.title: DDSN: A Physics-Aware Decoupled Dual-Stream Network for Speech Packet Loss Concealment
items.authors: Hao Tian(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Yonghui Liu(Fanvil Link Technology Co., Ltd); Jianbing Liu(Fanvil Link Technology Co., Ltd); Kai Niu(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Zhiqiang He(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications)
items.abstract: Packet loss concealment (PLC) restores high-fidelity speech from impaired signals in real-time communication. Existing frequency-domain methods typically process real and imaginary spectra jointly. This coupled modeling overlooks the distinct wrapped phase and magnitude characteristics, causing phase misalignment and structural artifacts. We propose a Wrapped-Phase-Aware Decoupled Dual-Stream Network (DDSN) that explicitly separates magnitude and phase modeling. Using independent streams, DDSN adapts to the specific characteristics of spectral energy and temporal alignment. To facilitate interaction, our Scaled Asymmetric Residual Guidance (SARG) mechanism uses magnitude priors to guide phase reconstruction. A manifold-constrained trigonometric representation maintains the topological consistency of the phase. Experimental results demonstrate DDSN performs favorably against established baselines, maintaining stable reconstruction during long burst losses.

items.title: A Causal Reference-Enhanced Keep-Speech Active Noise Control Method
items.authors: Li Rao(Nanjing University); Xiaobin Rong(Nanjing University; Nanjing Institute of Advanced AI); Yu Sun(Samsung Electronics (China)); Yiming He(Nanjing University); Kai Chen(Nanjing University); Haishan Zou(Nanjing University); Jing Lu(Nanjing University; Nanjing Institute of Advanced AI)
items.abstract: This paper proposes a causal, low-latency reference-enhanced keep-speech active noise control (KSANC) method, in which a deep neural network is used to enhance the reference signal by suppressing speech components while retaining noise. As a result, speech components in the error signal can be effectively preserved after control. The proposed method is validated through experiments using measured headphone impulse responses. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves speech intelligibility and speech quality in noisy conversational scenarios for headphone applications, compared with all baselines. Moreover, the method exhibits robustness to different speech signals and directions, noise types and directions, as well as varying signal-to-noise ratios. Listening examples are available at https://github.com/RaoLi666/RSE_KSANC.git.

items.title: Active Noise Control With a Gain Constraint for Micro-Loudspeakers
items.authors: Zhenhua Cheng(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Yi Zhou(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Yin Liu(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Yu Zhao(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Liming Shi(Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications)
items.abstract: The fixed-filter methods are widely employed in active noise control (ANC) systems due to their computational efficiency. They are typically designed to minimize the mean squared sound pressure at the error microphone, thereby attenuating disturbance components across the entire frequency spectrum. Due to the limited low-frequency reproduction capability of micro loudspeakers, this approach is prone to causing mechanical over-excursion. One solution is to cascade a high-pass filter before or after the control filter to limit the power of the output signal. But the group delay introduced by this filter increases the electronic latency. This paper proposes an ANC method with frequency-response gain constraints, where gain constraints are imposed on both the low-frequency range and the target noise reduction (NR) frequency range of the control filter's frequency response. Simulation and experimental results confirm the effectiveness of our proposed method in terms of NR performance.

items.title: DiffVQE: Hybrid Diffusion Voice Quality Enhancement Under Acoustic Echo and Noise
items.authors: Haljan Lugo(Technische Universität Braunschweig); Ernst Seidel(Technische Universität Braunschweig); Pejman Mowlaee(GN Advanced Science); Ziyue Zhao(GN Advanced Science); Tim Fingscheidt(Technische Universität Braunschweig)
items.abstract: Acoustic echo and background noise pose challenges on speech enhancement in hands-free systems and speakerphones. Discriminatively trained end-to-end methods represent a powerful solution for joint acoustic echo control (AEC) and denoising. However, with the advent of generative methods, diffusion-based approaches have seen remarkable performance in speech enhancement tasks. In this work, to the best of our knowledge, we provide the first (still non-causal) diffusion-based AEC model (DiffVQE) that is reproducible in terms of topology, training data, and training framework. So far, without employing diffusion, Microsoft's discriminative DeepVQE model has been shown to excel any of the ICASSP 2023 AEC Challenge entries achieving remarkable performance. Using data from the Interspeech 2025 URGENT Challenge for a diverse, high-quality training dataset, our DiffVQE excels DeepVQE both in echo and noise control performance, as well as in computational complexity and model size.

items.title: HybridCodec: Fast Dual-Stream, Semantically Enhanced Neural Audio Codec
items.authors: Arjun Gangwar(Indian Institute of Technology); S Umesh(Indian Institute of Technology)
items.abstract: The popularity of neural audio codecs as speech tokenizers has surged with the advent of Multimodal Large Language Models. New codec architectures with semantic and acoustic disentanglement have emerged. There are two main approaches to introduce semantic information into codec models: one distills semantic information from SSL representations into the first RVQ layer, while the other maintains separate streams for semantic and acoustic features. We propose HybridCodec, a unified architecture that combines both paradigms. It employs separate semantic and acoustic branches while distilling SSL representations into the semantic stream. This design ensures strong disentanglement without requiring an SSL model during inference. HybridCodec shows superior semantic specialization (RVQ-1) on in-domain test set and competitive reconstruction (RVQ-all). We demonstrate its robustness in out-of-domain and zero-shot cross-lingual settings, achieving a 3x speedup over existing dual-stream models.

items.title: WavSLM: Single-Stream Speech Language Modeling via WavLM Distillation
items.authors: Luca Della Libera(Concordia University; Mila-Quebec AI Institute); Cem Subakan(Universite Laval; Concordia University; Mila-Quebec AI Institute); Mirco Ravanelli(Concordia University; Mila-Quebec AI Institute)
items.abstract: Large language models show that simple autoregressive training can yield scalable and coherent generation, but extending this paradigm to speech remains challenging due to the entanglement of semantic and acoustic information. Most existing speech language models rely on text supervision, hierarchical token streams, or complex hybrid architectures, departing from the single-stream generative pretraining paradigm that has proven effective in text. In this work, we introduce WavSLM, a speech language model trained by quantizing and distilling self-supervised WavLM representations into a single codebook and optimizing an autoregressive next-chunk prediction objective. WavSLM jointly models semantic and acoustic information within a single token stream without text supervision or text pretraining. Despite its simplicity, it achieves competitive performance on consistency benchmarks and speech generation while using fewer parameters, less training data, and supporting streaming inference.

items.title: VOSSA: Voiceprint Optimization for Streaming Speech Architectures
items.authors: Mu-Ruei Tseng(Texas A&M University); Waris Quamer(Texas A&M University); Ghady Nasrallah(Texas A&M University); Ricardo Gutierrez-Osuna(Texas A&M University)
items.abstract: Real-time voice conversion (VC) systems commonly rely on pretrained speaker embeddings from automatic speaker verification (ASV) models. While effective for speaker discrimination, these embeddings are trained to remain stable across phonetic and prosodic variations within-speaker, which may conflict with frame-level acoustic generation in streaming constraints. To address this issue, we propose VOSSA (Voiceprint Optimization for Streaming Speech Architectures), a speaker representation framework that extracts speaker information from intermediate content encoder layers and aggregates using attentive statistics pooling. The embedding is trained jointly with VC objectives, removing the need for a separate speaker encoder. Across six datasets, VOSSA improves F0 dynamics and vowel-discriminative acoustic cues while maintaining comparable NISQA-MOS, WER, and speaker similarity. Perceptual tests further indicate improvements in naturalness, speaker similarity, intelligibility, and vibrancy.

items.title: MeanVC 2: Robust Low-Latency Streaming Zero-Shot Voice Conversion
items.authors: Guobin Ma(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Yuxuan Xia(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Yuepeng Jiang(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Dake Guo(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Hanke Xie(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Jingbin Hu(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Yanbo Wang(The University of New South Wales); Lei Xie(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Pengcheng Zhu(WeNet Open Source Community)
items.abstract: Streaming zero-shot voice conversion (VC) has become increasingly popular due to its potential for real-time applications. The recently proposed MeanVC achieves lightweight streaming zero-shot VC, but it has several limitations: its chunkwise autoregressive denoising doubles the effective training sequence length, conversion quality degrades under small-chunk settings, and its timbre encoder directly relies on reference melspectrograms, making it sensitive to reference audio quality. To address these limitations we propose MeanVC 2. We introduce future-receptive chunking (FRC), which explicitly schedules past and future receptive fields across diffusion transformer decoder layers and removes clean-chunk teacher forcing. By incorporating bounded future context, FRC enables stable conversion with a 40 ms chunk size. We further introduce a universal timbre token encoder, which constructs a timbre representation from a global speaker embedding and retrieves fine-grained timbre cues via cross-attention, improving robustness to low-quality references and enhancing zero-shot speaker similarity. Experimental results show that MeanVC 2 significantly outperforms MeanVC, while reducing latency from 211 ms to 110 ms. Audio samples are publicly available. The source code will be publicly released.

items.title: FlashTTS: Fast Streaming TTS with MTP Acceleration and X-pred Mean Flow Distillation
items.authors: Hanke Xie(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Xiaming Ren(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Dake Guo(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Ruonan You(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Wenhao Li(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Jingbin Hu(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Guobin Ma(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Huakang Chen(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.); Kejie Xu(Huawei); Rui Huang(Huawei); Weiguo Tan(Huawei); Xianrong Wang(Huawei); Lei Xie(Northwestern Polytech. Univ.)
items.abstract: Recent progress in speech dialogue systems requires text-to-Speech (TTS) models to be faster and more responsive. Modern speech dialogue systems impose two primary requirements on TTS models: low latency and support for streaming inputs and outputs. However, most existing single-codebook LLM-based TTS methods rely on multi-stage pipelines that lack native streaming capabilities. These systems typically suffer from high end-to-end latency due to slow autoregressive prediction and multi-step flow matching. To address these limitations, we propose FlashTTS, an open-source and low-latency streaming TTS framework. FlashTTS introduces a lagged multi-track architecture that natively processes streaming text and speech inputs, thereby eliminating the need for sentence-level buffering. To accelerate acoustic generation, we integrate parallel Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) with an X-pred mean flow matching decoder. This configuration achieves high-fidelity token-to-mel generation in exactly two function evaluations (2-NFE). By jointly optimizing input processing and decoding efficiency, FlashTTS offers a practical foundation for real-time speech dialogue systems. Experiments show that FlashTTS substantially reduces First-Packet Latency to 325ms compared to robust streaming baselines, all while preserving strong zero-shot voice cloning and cross-lingual intelligibility. Speech samples are available. The model code and checkpoints will be released as open source.

items.title: Prosodic Boundary-Aware Streaming Generation for LLM-Based TTS with Streaming Text Input
items.authors: Changsong Liu(Nanyang Technological University); Tianrui Wang(Nanyang Technological University; Tianjin University); Ye Ni(Nanyang Technological University; Southeast University); Yizhou Peng(Nanyang Technological University); Eng Siong Chng(Nanyang Technological University)
items.abstract: Streaming TTS that receives streaming text is essential for interactive systems, yet this scheme faces two major challenges: unnatural prosody due to missing lookahead and long-form collapse due to unbounded context. We propose a prosodic-boundary-aware post-training strategy, adapting a pre-trained LLM-based TTS model using weakly time-aligned data. Specifically, the model is adapted to learn early stopping at specified content boundaries when provided with limited future text. During inference, a sliding-window prompt carries forward previous text and speech tokens, ensuring bounded context and seamless concatenation. Evaluations show our method outperforms CosyVoice-Style interleaved baseline in both short and long-form scenarios. In long-text synthesis, especially, it achieves a 66.2% absolute reduction in word error rate (from 71.0% to 4.8%) and increases speaker and emotion similarity by 16.1% and 1.5% relatively, offering a robust solution for streaming TTS with incremental text.

items.title: CTC-TTS: LLM-Based Dual-Streaming Text-to-Speech with CTC Alignment
items.authors: Hanwen Liu(Xinjiang University); Saierdaer Yusuyin(Xinjiang University); Hao Huang(Xinjiang University); Zhijian Ou(Tsinghua University)
items.abstract: Large-language-model (LLM)-based text-to-speech (TTS) systems can generate natural speech, but most are not designed for low-latency dual-streaming synthesis. High-quality dual-streaming TTS depends on accurate text-speech alignment and well-designed training sequences that balance synthesis quality and latency. Prior work often relies on GMM-HMM based forced-alignment toolkits (e.g., MFA), which are pipeline-heavy and less flexible than neural aligners; fixed-ratio interleaving of text and speech tokens struggles to capture text-speech alignment regularities. We propose CTC-TTS, which replaces MFA with a CTC based aligner and introduces a bi-word based interleaving strategy. Two variants are designed: CTC-TTS-L (token concatenation along the sequence length) for higher quality and CTC-TTS-F (feature-dimension embedding stacking) for lower latency. Experiments show that CTC-TTS outperforms fixed-ratio interleaving and MFA-based baselines on streaming synthesis and zero-shot tasks.

items.title: PF-D2M: A Pose-free Diffusion Model for Universal Dance-to-Music Generation
items.authors: Jaekwon Im(KAIST); Natalia Polouliakh(Sony CSL Tokyo); Taketo Akama(Sony CSL Tokyo)
items.abstract: Dance-to-music generation aims to generate music that is aligned with dance movements. Existing approaches typically rely on body motion features extracted from a single human dancer and limited dance-to-music datasets, which restrict their performance and applicability to real-world scenarios involving multiple dancers and non-human dancers. In this paper, we propose PF-D2M, a universal diffusion-based dance-to-music generation model that incorporates visual features extracted from dance videos. PF-D2M is trained with a progressive training strategy that effectively addresses data scarcity and generalization challenges. Both objective and subjective evaluations show that PF-D2M achieves state-of-the-art performance in dance-music alignment and music quality. Samples of PF-D2M are available at https://jakeoneijk.github.io/pfd2m_project

items.title: Streaming T5-based Text-to-Speech Synthesis with Limited Lookahead
items.authors: Muyang Du(NVIDIA, China); Jason Roche(NVIDIA, USA); Junjie Lai(NVIDIA, China)
items.abstract: Streaming text-to-speech synthesis in cascaded LLM-TTS systems still faces latency challenges as most TTS models require full context before initiating generation. We present S5-TTS, a Streaming variant of T5-TTS that enables low-latency, word-by-word incremental speech synthesis through encoder-decoder language modeling and monotonic alignment learning. S5-TTS begins generating speech immediately after receiving the first few words, substantially reducing end-to-end response latency. To maintain quality under limited lookahead, we introduce a lookahead-causal masking mechanism with Conv-based auxiliary attention that preserves intelligibility and speaker similarity, and employ interleaved multi-source distillation to further restore naturalness. Experiments show that S5-TTS achieves comparable quality to full-context T5-TTS, supports zero-shot synthesis with high speaker similarity, and significantly reduces end-to-end latency for practical conversational AI systems.

items.title: Learning to Wait: Real Streaming Speech-to-Text Translation with an LLM
items.authors: Shucong Zhang(Samsung, AI Center-Cambridge); Titouan Parcollet(Samsung, AI Center-Cambridge); Rogier van Dalen(Samsung, AI Center-Cambridge)
items.abstract: A streaming speech-to-text translation system outputs tokens as the audio comes in. The state of the art for streaming speech translation with an LLM is Bestow. Bestow's wait policy is fixed: it outputs tokens at a fixed cadence irrespective of the contents of the audio. On a test set, it often seems to perform well, but not in the real world. If no speech is heard immediately after the microphone is opened, then the fixed policy will force tokens out and produce hallucinations; if the speaker speaks fast, the system will fall behind. This paper instead proposes a wait policy that learns when to wait for more audio and when to emit tokens. On a test set, the model that uses this policy achieve better quality and/or better latency. Moreover, it is not susceptible to hallucinations for real-world data.

items.title: Leveraging Audio-LLMs to Filter Speech-to-Speech Training Data
items.authors: Qixu Chen(The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: Large-scale mined corpora provide abundant training data for end-to-end speech-to-speech translation (S2ST) but may contain noise, misalignment, and semantic errors. Filtering noisy data is crucial to maintain robust speech translation performance. We study how to train an audio-language model to make keep/drop decisions on paired speech directly from audio. To obtain reliable supervision without manual labels, we adopt a scalable two-stage Rank→Distill strategy. A lightweight ranker generates keep/drop pseudo-labels from noisy speech pairs, then trains an audio large language model to predict keep/drop directly from raw paired speech. The resulting model jointly captures acoustic fidelity and cross-lingual semantic consistency for the selection of speech-conditioned data. Experiments on CVSS-C and SpeechMatrix show consistent improvements over unfiltered training, yielding up to +1.4 ASR-BLEU for end-to-end S2ST.

items.title: POTSA: A Cross-Lingual Speech Alignment Framework for Speech-to-Text Translation
items.authors: Xuanchen Li(Tianjin University); Chenrui Cui(Tianjin University); Tianrui Wang(Tianjin University; NTU Singapore); Meng Ge(Tianjin University); Zikang Huang(Tianjin University); Yizhou Peng(NTU Singapore); Jin Li(Tianjin University); Yuheng Lu(Tianjin University); Yu Jiang(Tianjin University); Nyima Tashi(Tibet University); Longbiao Wang(Tianjin University; Huiyan Technology); Jianwu Dang(Chinese Academy of Sciences)
items.abstract: Speech Large Language Models have achieved breakthroughs in multilingual speech-to-text translation. However, existing approaches often overlook semantic commonalities across source languages, leading to biased translation performance. In this work, we propose POTSA (Parallel Optimal Transport for Speech Alignment), a new framework based on cross-lingual parallel speech pairs and Optimal Transport, designed to bridge high- and low-resource translation gaps. First, we introduce a Bias Compensation module to coarsely align initial speech representations. Second, we impose token-level OT constraints on a Q-Former using parallel pairs to establish fine-grained representation consistency. Then, we apply a layer scheduling strategy to focus OT constraints on semantically beneficial layers. Experiments on FLEURS show our method achieves SOTA performance, with +1.29 BLEU over five common languages and +2.93 BLEU on zero-shot languages, using only 10 hours of parallel speech per language.

items.title: Automated Gradient-Driven Parameter Sharing for Low-Resource Multilingual Speech-to-Text Translation
items.authors: Ruiyan Sun(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Satoshi Nakamura(The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: Multilingual S2T models typically use uniform sharing due to insufficient training data, which can lead to representation conflicts in low-resource scenarios. We present a gradient-driven framework that automatically discovers optimal parameter sharing configurations by analyzing inter-language gradient behaviors. Our approach integrates clustering for grouping, similarity analysis for shared-private ratios, and joint SVD with regularized CCA for subspace calibration. On four low-resource language pairs using the SeamlessM4T-Medium model, our Gradient-Driven Parameter Sharing (GDPS) framework achieves consistent improvements.

items.title: Multilingual Multi-Speaker Unit Vocoders: A Systematic Analysis of Discrete Speech Representations
items.authors: Naman Kothari(National Institute of Technology); Arjun Gangwar(Indian Institute of Technology); Adarsh Arigala(Indian Institute of Technology); S Umesh(Indian Institute of Technology)
items.abstract: Discrete speech units obtained via k-means clustering of self supervised embeddings entangle phonetic, speaker, and language information, causing speaker mixing and cross-lingual interference in multilingual multi-speaker speech generation. Despite growing use in Audio LLMs and speech to speech systems, unit vocoders remain underexplored. We analyze a BigVGAN based unit vocoder, across four Indian languages. We study the interaction between cluster size and conditioning strategies using WER, speaker similarity, and unit level metrics. Results show that cluster size governs intelligibility by improving phonetic discriminability, while explicit speaker conditioning is indispensable for preventing identity collapse. Language supervision yields further gains mainly at lower cluster sizes where units remain ambiguous. Our analysis shows similar phonemes across languages collapse to the same cluster IDs at smaller inventories, with larger clusters progressively separating them.

items.title: Evaluation of forced alignment of code-mixed speech: the case of Hindi-English
items.authors: Ayushi Pandey(Karya); Pamir Gogoi(Karya); Kevin Tang(Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf; University of Florida )
items.abstract: Code-mixed speech poses unique challenges to forced alignment: expanded inventories, orthographic errors, and speaker variation. We evaluate forced alignment of Hindi-English code-mixed speech using the Montreal Forced Aligner. We address 2 problems: (1) free variation involving native vs non-native pairs and (2) phonemic boundary detection for mid-utterance English words. Bootstrapping strategies substantially outperform unmodified lexicons. Acoustic models trained on sentence-level code-mixed data achieve a mean error of 4.15ms, ie. ten times lower than monolingual Hindi (38.18ms) or isolated English (37.58ms) alternatives. Principled lexicon design and code-mixed training data are both essential for reliable alignment of bilingual speech.

items.title: Does Translation-Enhanced Speech Encoder Pre-training Affect Speech LLMs?
items.authors: Tomoya Mizumoto(SB Intuitions); Yusuke Fujita(SB Intuitions)
items.abstract: Connecting a pre-trained speech encoder to a Large Language Model (LLM) is the standard architecture for building Speech LLMs. However, a structural misalignment exists between phonetically anchored encoders and semantically organized LLMs. To bridge this divide, the encoder benefits from objectives that emphasize semantic understanding over surface-level sound recognition. We argue that speech translation provides a principled way to achieve this. Unlike transcription, translation requires capturing meaning beyond phonetic similarity, since the source speech and the target text do not systematically align at the phonetic level. We experimentally evaluate the impact of incorporating translation objectives into speech encoder pre-training. Our results demonstrate that translation-enhanced pre-training significantly improves cross-modal integration and leads to superior performance across downstream Speech LLM tasks.

items.title: PiDA: Phonetically-Informed Data Augmentation for Robust Vietnamese Speech Translation
items.authors: Giang Son Nguyen(VinUniversity); Tung X. Nguyen(VinUniversity); Hieu Minh Truong(VinUniversity); Nhu Vo(VinUniversity; University of Technology Sydney); Wray Buntine(VinUniversity; Monash University); Dung D. Le(VinUniversity)
items.abstract: Cascaded speech translation (ST) systems suffer from error propagation when Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) outputs incorrect transcripts. We present the first systematic categorization of ASR errors for Vietnamese ST, classifying substitution errors by phonetic cause and quantifying their impact on downstream Neural Machine Translation (NMT) performance using Linear Mixed-Effects Modelling. We confirm that most ASR substitution errors arise from phonetic confusions rather than random noise, and that these phonetic errors significantly degrade ST quality. Motivated by this finding, we propose Phonetically-Informed Data Augmentation (PiDA), which generates ASR-like corruptions by substituting words with phonetically similar alternatives using phonetic word embeddings. Fine-tuning on a PiDA-augmented version of FLEURS Vietnamese-English improves translation of erroneous ASR outputs (up to +2.04 BLEU over standard fine-tuning) while also slightly improving clean-text performance.

items.title: MoVE: Translating Laughter and Tears via Mixture of Vocalization Experts in Speech-to-Speech Translation
items.authors: Szu-Chi Chen(National Taiwan University); I-Ning Tsai(National Taiwan University); Yi-Cheng Lin(National Taiwan University); Sung-Feng Huang(NVIDIA); Hung-yi Lee(National Taiwan University; NTU AI-CoRE)
items.abstract: Recent Speech-to-Speech Translation (S2ST) systems achieve strong semantic accuracy yet consistently strip away non-verbal vocalizations (NVs), such as laughter and crying that convey pragmatic intent, which severely limits real-world utility. We address this via three contributions. First, we propose a synthesis pipeline for building scalable expressive datasets to overcome the data scarcity limitation. Second, we propose MoVE, a Mixture-of-LoRA-Experts architecture with expressive-specialized adapters and a soft-weighting router that blends experts for capturing hybrid expressive states. Third, we show pretrained AudioLLMs enable striking data efficiency: 30 minutes of curated data is enough for strong performance. On English-Chinese S2ST, while comparing with strong baselines, MoVE reproduces target NVs in 76% of cases and achieves the highest human-rated naturalness and emotional fidelity among all compared systems, where existing S2ST systems preserve at most 14% of NVs.

items.title: Cross-Modal Robustness Transfer (CMRT): Training Robust Speech Translation Models Using Adversarial Text
items.authors: Abderrahmane Issam(Maastricht University); Yusuf Can Semerci(Maastricht University); Jan Scholtes(Maastricht University); Gerasimos Spanakis(Maastricht University)
items.abstract: End-to-End Speech Translation (E2E-ST) has made significant progress but often relies on curated datasets, overlooking challenges like robustness to inflectional morphology variations common in non-native and dialectal speech. In this work, we adapt an adversarial attack targeting inflectional morphology from the text domain to speech and demonstrate that E2E-ST models are highly vulnerable. While adversarial fine-tuning improves robustness in text, generating adversarial speech data is computationally difficult. To address this, we propose Cross-Modal Robustness Transfer (CMRT), a method that transfers robustness from text to the speech modality without requiring adversarial speech data. Experiments across four language directions show that CMRT improves adversarial robustness by over 3 BLEU points on average while maintaining performance on clean data.

items.title: YODAS v3: Over 1 Million Hours of High-Bandwidth, Stereophonic, Multilingual Speech
items.authors: William Chen(Carnegie Mellon University); Shinnosuke Takamichi(Keio University); Sayaka Shiota(Tokyo Metropolitan University); Satoru Fukayama(National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technolog (AIST)); Samuele Cornell(Carnegie Mellon University); Shinji Watanabe(Carnegie Mellon University)
items.abstract: We present YODAS v3, a weakly-labeled speech corpus containing over 1.1 million hours of 48kHz multi-channel audio in 147 languages, released under a CC BY 3.0 license. YODAS v3 is not only the largest open speech dataset to date, but also the first truly large-scale speech corpus with high-fidelity stereo audio. We first provide the collection methodology for the corpus, where we introduce new techniques for gathering language-balanced speech data. The effectiveness of our approach is shown by the language distribution of the crawled data: 22 languages in YODAS v3 have over 10K hours and 73 languages have over 5K hours of data. We then conduct extensive analyses on the composition of the data, such as the distribution of languages, audio quality, and transcription quality. Finally, we train baseline speech recognition and neural codec models to show the effectiveness of the dataset. Download at https://huggingface.co/datasets/espnet/yodas3.

items.title: Inverse Text Normalization in Romanian: A Comparative Study of Rule-Based, Neural, and Large Language Model Approaches
items.authors: Oana Sirbu(University of Bucharest); Alexandra Diaconu(University of Bucharest); Sergiu Nisioi(University of Bucharest); Bogdan Alexe(University of Bucharest; Gheorghe Mihoc-Caius Iacob Institute of Mathematical Statistics and Applied Mathematics of the Romanian Academy)
items.abstract: Inverse Text Normalization (ITN) converts spoken-form automatic speech recognition transcripts into standardized written text and is a critical post-processing step in speech systems. We present a comparative study of ITN in Romanian, evaluating rule-based grammars, neural sequence-to-sequence models, fine-tuned multilingual transformers, and large language models under a unified evaluation framework that separates copy and normalization errors. Experiments on 24k manually annotated spoken-written pairs, including out-of-distribution evaluation, reveal distinct trade-offs. Deterministic grammars provide high precision and efficiency but limited coverage, while neural models benefit from pretraining yet exhibit numerical instability. Few-shot LLM prompting achieves near-human accuracy and stronger cross-domain generalization at higher computational cost. Our results clarify accuracy-efficiency trade-offs and provide practical guidance for deploying ITN in speech pipelines.

items.title: Audiovisual CXMI: Scene-based Context Tagging for Spoken Language Translation Evaluation
items.authors: Dayeon Ku(Dept. of EECS); Hwayoung Park(Dept. of AI Convergence, Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology); Hong Kook Kim(Dept. of EECS; Dept. of AI Convergence, Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology; AunionAI Co., Ltd.)
items.abstract: Existing metrics assess translation quality at the sentence level but cannot measure how well a machine translation model utilizes context. Conditional Cross-Mutual Information (CXMI) quantifies context usage, yet considers only text, missing audiovisual cues that human translators exploit. We propose Audiovisual CXMI (AV-CXMI), an extension of CXMI with scene-based audiovisual tags extracted from video. Our framework first segments video into scenes via visual boundary detection refined by speaker analysis. Next, we extract structured tags capturing six contextual categories from multimodal streams, and finally, evaluate translation quality conditioned on the extracted tags. items.title: Steps toward a wearable-informed model of real-world listening effort and fatigue among adults with hearing loss
items.authors: David Meng(National Acoustic Laboratories); Marisa Poulos(National Acoustic Laboratories); Erin O'Neill(GN Advanced Science); Qi Yang(GN Advanced Science); Ivan Iotzov(GN Advanced Science); Jorge Mejia(National Acoustic Laboratories)
items.abstract: Listening-associated fatigue is common in hearing loss, even with advanced hearing aids, and likely arises from cumulative listening effort. Current hearing-aid algorithms adapt to acoustics but not to users' moment-to-moment experience. We tested whether consumer wearables can capture listening effort and fatigue in daily life. Forty-six adults with hearing loss (23 hearing-aid users, 23 non-users) completed a 7-10 day field study using Apple Watch-based ecological momentary assessments (EMAs), passive heart-rate and sound monitoring, and daily phone surveys. Participants engaged well: without prompts, they logged check-ins comparable to prior phone-based EMA studies. Using wearable-informed features, we classified high listening effort and high fatigue with accuracies of 68% and 76%. Wearable-informed measures of effort and fatigue appear feasible in everyday contexts and may support future real-time adaptive hearing technology and longitudinal monitoring.

items.title: Towards a Stochastic DNN Approximation of Cochlear Implant Auditory Models
items.authors: Theresa Hartmann(Ruhr-Universität Bochum); Ian C. Bruce(McMaster University); Benjamin Lentz(Ruhr-Universität Bochum); Rainer Martin(Ruhr-Universität Bochum); Anil Nagathil(Ruhr-Universität Bochum; McMaster University)
items.abstract: This paper presents a data-driven approximation of an electrical-stimulation auditory model using deep neural networks. In contrast to existing deterministic approaches, the proposed method models stochastic characteristics of electrically evoked neural responses. A hierarchical vector-quantized variational autoencoder is trained to map spectrograms with Greenwood-type frequency resolution to parameters of a Gamma distribution which are used to sample probabilistic mean-rate neurograms. We performed an objective evaluation based on the Jensen-Shannon divergence and the neurogram similarity index measure, quantifying distributional and structural similarity. The evaluation shows that the model effectively captures the global spectro-temporal structure and essential stochastic properties of the auditory model, especially at low and mid frequencies. Overall, this work constitutes a promising step towards a time-efficient stochastic approximation of electrical-stimulation auditory models.

items.title: WhisperVC: Decoupled Cross-Domain Alignment and Speech Generation for Low-Resource Whisper-to-Normal Conversion
items.authors: Dong Liu(Wuhan University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Juan Liu(Wuhan University); Wei Ju(OPPO); Yao Tian(OPPO); Ming Li(The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Wuhan University)
items.abstract: Whispered speech lacks vocal-fold excitation, making the intelligible conversion challenging. We propose WhisperVC, a three-stage framework for low-resource Whisper-to-Normal (W2N) conversion that decouples cross-domain alignment from speech generation. Stage 1 uses limited paired whisper-normal data with a content encoder and a Conformer-based variational autoencoder (VAE) with soft-DTW alignment to learn domain-invariant semantic representations. Stage 2, trained only on normal speech, employs a Length-Channel Aligner and a two-stage speaker-conditioned mel generator for timbre and prosody modeling. Stage 3 fine-tunes a HiFi-GAN vocoder for waveform synthesis. Experimental results on AISHELL6-Whisper show competitive quality (DNSMOS 3.07, UTMOS 2.83, CER 16.93%) and WavLM speaker similarity (0.95). The framework also supports privacy-preserving communication as well as nonvocal communication and a rehabilitation tool for post-surgical vocal-fold patients. Samples are available online.

items.title: Bridging the Speech AI Accessibility Gap for Deaf and Hard of Hearing People
items.authors: Abraham Glasser(Gallaudet University); Christian Vogler(Gallaudet University); Raja Kushalnagar(Gallaudet University)
items.abstract: In this position paper, we, a team of Deaf signers who can and do use our voices, discuss how speech Artificial Intelligence (AI) services fail to account for the unique use and needs by Deaf and Hard of Hearing (DHH). DHH individuals often speak with "deaf accents" shaped by hearing loss and ethnicity. Current speech AI struggles with these nuances, creating barriers and failing to capture the rich meaning of speech compared to text. Through our lived experiences, we highlight essential design frameworks for future AI: UVG (Usability, Verifiability, Graceful Degradation) and FATE (Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, Ethics). We explore non-auditory verification, preserving DHH identity through personalized voices, and address the privacy, data, and community marginalization risks of developing AI without DHH input. By centering DHH perspectives, we advocate for inclusive, context-aware technologies that promote equitable communication in workplaces, social spaces, and beyond.

items.title: Emergence of Phonetic Representations in EMG-based Silent Speech Interfaces
items.authors: Guillaume Toussaint(SUPSI); Deborah Pereg(SUPSI); Kevin Scheck(University of Bremen); Tanja Schultz(University of Bremen); Jürgen Schmidhuber(SUPSI; KAUST Center of Generative AI); Michael Wand(SUPSI)
items.abstract: In this work, we investigate learned representations of a surface EMG-based silent speech interface trained for different tasks (speech synthesis, recognition, phone classification, unsupervised pretraining). We show that such systems develop phonetic representations even without explicit supervision, that incorporating a regression loss on acoustic targets is essential for producing intelligible synthetic speech, and we show that self-supervised contrastive learning alone results in a latent space which does not yield measurable improvements in speech synthesis or phone classification tasks.

items.title: Investigating ASR for Low-Intelligibility Dysarthric Speech
items.authors: Jinuk Kwon(University of Texas at Austin; Dell Medical School, University of Texas at Austin); Beiming Cao(University of Texas at Austin); Carl Sigmond(University of Texas at Austin); Kristin Teplansky(University of Texas at Austin); Jun Wang(University of Texas at Austin; Dell Medical School, University of Texas at Austin)
items.abstract: Despite the recent advances in automatic speech recognition (ASR) for dysarthria, it remains challenging for low-intelligibility speech, as most studies used datasets that are dominated by mild to moderate dysarthric speech. In this study, we investigated ASR for severe dysarthria by utilizing a unique, large dataset from an individual with low-intelligibility speech. First, we implemented a bidirectional long short-term memory-hidden Markov model (BLSTM-HMM) and fine-tuned large-scale pretrained Whisper models in speaker-dependent settings. Both models achieved substantially low word error rates (< 14%), indicating severe dysarthria can be effectively modelled with sufficient data. Second, we generalized a fine-tuned Whisper model to other patients, achieving a 6.4 percentage point improvement for severe dysarthria compared to the non-fine-tuned model without performance degradation for mild and moderate cases, suggesting the potential of generalization of ASR for severe dysarthria.

items.title: What Counts as an Error? Dual-Reference Benchmarking for Atypical ASR
items.authors: Hawau Olamide Toyin(MBZUAI); Srinivasan Umesh(IIT Madras); Hanan Aldarmaki(MBZUAI)
items.abstract: ASR systems have been often reported to underperform on atypical speech. An often conflated compounding factor is the existence of two valid transcription references: verbatim (actual produced speech, including repetitions/prolongations) and intended (the canonical form of the text with disfluencies removed) in atypical speech recognition depending on context and use-case. Most ASR evaluations conflate this duality into a single ground truth and reward systems that delete disfluencies, ignoring verbatim faithfulness. We benchmark 11 ASR models from encoder-decoder, CTC and transducer families using both verbatim and intended references on atypical stuttered speech as a case study. Our quantitative assessment underlines the disparity in model performance and rankings using the two transcript styles. Through this analysis, we highlight the importance of selecting a suitable transcription reference for valid model selection depending on the use-case, particularly for atypical ASR.

items.title: Relative Importance of Formants to the Intelligibility of Vocoded Speech in Cochlear Implant Simulation
items.authors: Ying Cai(Southern University of Science and Technology); Yuting Ding(Southern University of Science and Technology); Xuefei Wang(Southern University of Science and Technology); Fei Chen(Southern University of Science and Technology)
items.abstract: This study examined the relative significance of formants for the intelligibility of vocoded speech, which simulates the speech processing of cochlear implant (CI) speech processors. Mandarin sentences were edited to generate sine-wave speech that retained only the trajectories of the first three formants. Three experimental conditions were designed: each removed one of the first three formant trajectories, leaving two formant trajectories intact. Results indicated that the second formant trajectory contributed most to intelligibility, while the third had the least impact, aligning with findings from wideband (non-vocoded) speech. However, vocoder model parameters (e.g., envelope cut-off frequency and number of frequency bands) regulated this relative importance. These findings provide insights for optimizing CI speech processor design to deliver critical spectral information for improving CI users' speech understanding.

items.title: Towards Personalized Federated Learning for Dysarthric Speech Recognition
items.authors: Tao Zhong(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Mengzhe Geng(National Research Council Canada); Jiajun Deng(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Shujie Hu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Xunying Liu(The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: Speech recognition is challenging for dysarthric speakers. While federated learning (FL)-based ASR can be an effective tool for protecting privacy, it suffers from heterogeneity issues caused by speaker variability. Forcing all speakers to share the same model components can be suboptimal under such heterogeneity, making personalization a promising direction; however, related research on dysarthric speech remains limited. To this end, this paper explores two aggregation strategies to achieve personalization, including the parameter-based averaging strategy and the embedding-based averaging strategy. Experiments on UASpeech and TORGO show that the proposed methods outperform the baseline regularized FedAvg by statistically significant WER reductions of up to 0.99% absolute (3.15% relative) on UASpeech and 0.56% absolute (4.73% relative) on TORGO, respectively.

items.title: Shared Phone-Level Neural Representations of Auditory Perception and ‘Inner Voice’ Production: One-to-One Mapping using a Single-Subject EEG Corpus of Heard and Imagined Natural Speech
items.authors: Scott Wellington(University of Bath); Oliver Watts(SpeakUnique Ltd); Damien Coyle(University of Bath); Benjamin Metcalfe(University of Bath)
items.abstract: We present a novel paradigm that enables the collection of time-aligned heard and imagined natural fully-connected speech, and use it to collect over 22 hours of single-participant EEG. We make these data publicly available. We present results of an experiment that shows how these data can be used to probe the extent to which similar neural processing underlies auditory perception and imagined speech production at the phonetic level. Specifically, we demonstrate that the evoked response potentials (ERPs) of phones elicited during imagined speech are closest in vector space to the ERPs of the corresponding phones for heard speech. We show that a weighted sum of different frequency sub-bands can be calculated via convex quadratic optimisation to improve this one-to-one mapping between heard and imagined speech phones. Our findings suggest that the ‘inner voice’ has phone-level neural correlates; this can inform the direction of research into brain-computer interfaces for imagined speech.
